newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-DEFIANT BROWNE FAILS TO SAVE FOLLOW-ON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DEFIANT BROWNE FAILS TO SAVE FOLLOW-ON.

text.p: A brave 93 not out by
wicketkeeper Courtney Browne failed to save West Indies being
forced to follow on 227 runs behind on the third day of their
four-day match against an Australia XI at Bellerive Oval on
Sunday.
Browne's innings was the only bright spot in another dismal
day for West Indies ahead of the first test against Australia
starting in Brisbane on Friday.
His effort took West Indies to 317 in their first innings
after they had been in deep trouble at 82 for four overnight.
West Indies finished 227 runs behind Australia XI's first
innings of 544 for four declared.
West Indies were 102 for two in their second innings at the
close when Shivnarine Chanderpaul was 42 not out and
nightwatchman Ian Bishop one.
Browne, batting at number eight, at least gave West Indies a
chance of salvaging a draw which at one stage looked unlikely
when they were 179 for seven.
He and Nixon McLean briefly raised West Indies hopes of
avoiding the follow-on with a ninth wicket stand of 74 in 54
minutes, McLean hitting three fours and two sixes in scoring 41
from 27 balls.
Browne was denied what would have been only the second
century of the tour for West Indies when last man Patterson
Thompson was run out for one. Chanderpaul hit West Indies only
century of the tour against Western Australia in a three-day
match a week ago.
Pace bowlers Andrew Bichel and Anthony Stuart both extracted
bounce and movement from the pitch to take four wickets each.
Stuart then had opener Sherwin Campbell
caught behind by Adam Gilchrist for 22 in the second innings.
Fellow opener Robert Samuels made 34 before falling to
left-arm wrist-spinner Brad Hogg for 34.
